subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: After direct sibling Codex inspection and green exact-head workflow checks, should the 14 security-sensitive action revisions be accepted as one grouped update?
rationale: These actions execute across token, secret, publishing, scanning, and agent boundaries, and the repository’s protected security label plus mandatory Codex-source gate require explicit human ownership.

options.title: Approve after full proof
options.body: Accept the grouped update after rebasing, completing direct Codex contract inspection, and confirming the relevant workflows pass on the exact head.

options.title: Split the highest-risk pins
options.body: Separate Codex, token-minting, registry, and security-scanning actions into smaller PRs if grouped proof remains difficult to interpret.

options.title: Retain current pins
options.body: Close or supersede this update if the refreshed actions introduce unacceptable workflow or permission changes.

recommendation.title: Approve after full proof
recommendation.body: Accept the grouped update after rebasing, completing direct Codex contract inspection, and confirming the relevant workflows pass on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to release workflows and security-sensitive release operations.
